general_information.Description: "This course provides students in the Automotive Software and Intergrated Circuir Engineering field with a solid foundation in fundamental data structures and algorithms, focusing on applications in embedded and control systems used in vehicles. Topics include methods for efficiently storing, accessing, and processing data using structures such as linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, graphs, and hash tables; and algorithms for sorting, searching, and traversing trees and graphs. Special emphasis is placed on real-world automotive applications such as sensor data processing, engine queue management, pathfinding and mapping, and task scheduling in real-time embedded systems."
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend more than 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Promptly access to the FU CMS at http://cmshn.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information - Promptly access to the EduNext system at https://fu-edunext.fpt.edu.vn for all activity.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Overview fundamental Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) concepts such as encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism in C++

Complexity and Performance Analysis: 1. Understand and apply asymptotic analysis (Big-O, Ω, and Θ notation) to evaluate algorithm efficiency. 2. Differentiate between best-case, average-case, and worst-case complexity scenarios.
Be able to understand and apply Linked Lists and Dynamic Data Structures: Implement singly linked lists, doubly linked lists, circular lists in C++
Be able to understand Stacks, Queues, and Their Applications
Be able to understand recursion its applications
Be able to understand Sorting and Searching Algorithms

Understandable and applicable Trees and Binary Search Trees (BSTs) 1. Construct and manipulate binary search trees (BSTs), including insertion, deletion, and traversal. 2. Implement self-balancing trees (AVL trees, splay trees, and red-black trees) to maintain optimal performance. 3: Use heaps and priority queues for efficient data storage and retrieval.
Be able to understand and apply Graph theory
Be able to understand Hashing and Efficient Data Retrieval
Be able to understand Data Compression
Be able to understand String Matching Algorithms
